newsitem.title: USA: Holbrooke to return to Balkans next week.
newsitem.headline: Holbrooke to return to Balkans next week.

text.p: Former Bosnia peace negotiator Richard Holbrooke will visit the Balkans next week as part of a U.S. team that will press for implementation of the Dayton peace accord, the State Department said on Wednesday.
Spokesman James Foley said the delegation will be led by Robert Gelbard, U.S. special representative for Dayton implementation, and will visit Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia.

Foley said the mission will discuss U.S. concerns about implementation of the accords, which were reached in November 1995 largely thanks to the efforts of Holbrooke, who was an assistant secretary of state at the time.
Foley said the team will travel to the region on or about Aug. 6 and meet key Balkan leaders, including all parties to the Dayton accords. The itinerary was not complete, he added.

The team will press for "concrete action" on the accords, which while they ended the Bosnia war have failed to lead to the handover of most war criminals, the return of most refugees to their homes, or ethnic reconciliation.
Holbrooke quit government service in February 1996 to join Credit Suisse First Boston bank, a position he still holds. He was recently appointed a part-time U.S. envoy on the Cyprus problem.
